scope: behavioral primitives and focused tests only; no engine registration or certification

cards.name: Armed Dragon LV3
cards.effectSummary: During its controller's Standby Phase, it may send itself from the field to the GY to Special Summon Armed Dragon LV5 from that player's hand or Deck.

cards.name: Armed Dragon LV5
cards.effectSummary: It may send a monster from its controller's hand to the GY, then target one face-up opposing monster whose current ATK is no greater than the sent monster's original ATK and destroy it. During the End Phase, if it destroyed a monster by battle that turn, it may send itself to the GY to Special Summon Armed Dragon LV7 from that player's hand or Deck.

cards.name: Armed Dragon LV7
cards.effectSummary: Cannot be Normal Summoned/Set and must be Special Summoned by Armed Dragon LV5. It may send a monster from its controller's hand to the GY to destroy all face-up opposing monsters whose current ATK is no greater than the sent monster's original ATK.

twoVTwoAdaptation.privateHandAndDeck: only the resolving physical seat supplies discard and summon candidates
twoVTwoAdaptation.sharedField: the opposing team includes both opposing seats; the helper filters by controllerTeam
twoVTwoAdaptation.physicalOwnership: field cards sent to the GY retain physical owner routing; opponent monsters destroyed by effect route to their physical owner's team GY
twoVTwoAdaptation.nonTargeting: LV7 computes the eligible opposing field at resolution; it does not store target UIDs
twoVTwoAdaptation.attackComparison: discarded monster original/printed ATK is the threshold; opposing monsters current ATK is compared
twoVTwoAdaptation.summonCondition: LV7 is summoned by LV5; Level Up! may bypass the summon condition from hand/Deck, but the helper rejects Graveyard/banished sources

behavioralGroups: LV3 Standby Phase transition from Hand/Deck
LV5 End Phase transition only after same-turn battle destruction
private Hand/Deck ownership and physical owner routing
LV5 discard cost and single-target ATK threshold
LV5 target revalidation after activation while retaining paid cost
LV7 summon restriction and non-targeting board wipe
UID uniqueness and stale/invalid state rejection

rulingReference.authority: archived Edison format individual card rulings; historical reference, not current Konami-issued ruling authority
notes: LV5 targets a face-up monster and uses current ATK for the target check.
LV7 does not destroy face-down monsters and compares current opposing ATK with the discarded monster's original printed ATK.
Level Up! can bypass LV7's summoning condition from hand or Deck.
